issues.legal_issue: The Commissioner may revise an assessment only when the assessment order is both erroneous and prejudicial to the interests of the revenue.
material_facts: The assessing officer made a nil assessment and accepted the company’s description of the receipt as compensation for loss of agricultural income without supporting material or inquiry.
The company’s board resolution concerning the receipt was not before the assessing officer.
The Commissioner found that the receipt was not connected with agricultural activity and that the assessment order was erroneous and prejudicial to the revenue.
issues.conclusion: The Commissioner was justified in exercising revisionary jurisdiction because the assessment order was made without application of mind or inquiry and resulted in lawful tax not being assessed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 263(1) of the Income-tax Act, both conditions must be met: the assessment order must be erroneous and prejudicial to the interests of the revenue. An incorrect assumption of fact, incorrect application of law, or an order made without applying the mind may make an order erroneous. Prejudice is not limited to loss of tax, but a revenue loss alone does not suffice if the assessing officer adopted a course permissible in law or a sustainable view where two views were possible. The Court rejected the narrower approach in Venkatakrishna Rice Company v. Commissioner of Income-tax and referred to Dawjee Dadabhoy & Co. v. S.P. Jain, Commissioner of Income-tax v. T. Narayana Pai, Commissioner of Income-tax v. Gabriel India Ltd., Commissioner of Income-tax v. Smt. Minalben S. Parikh, Rampyari Devi Saraogi v. Commissioner of Income-tax, and Smt. Tara Devi Aggarwal v. Commissioner of Income-tax.

rule.if: revision_proceeding and assessment_without_inquiry and unsupported_income_characterization and lawful_tax_not_assessed

predicates.revision_proceeding: The matter concerns a commissioner’s exercise of supervisory revision over an assessment.
predicates.assessment_without_inquiry: The assessing officer accepted the relevant tax treatment without making an inquiry or applying the mind to the matter.
predicates.unsupported_income_characterization: The taxpayer’s description of a receipt was accepted without supporting material before the assessing officer.
predicates.lawful_tax_not_assessed: The assessment left income lawfully taxable unassessed.

issues.definition: When a revision proceeding concerns an assessment made without inquiry on an unsupported characterization and lawful tax was left unassessed, the commissioner may revise the assessment.

issues.legal_issue: A payment made in connection with extending the time for payment under a sale agreement is not agricultural income merely because it is described as compensation for loss of agricultural income.
material_facts: The company received payment after the purchaser sought extensions of time to pay instalments due under an agreement to buy a rubber plantation.
The payment was made in modification or relaxation of the contract terms, rather than for breach of contract.

The company’s agricultural operations had stopped before the receipt, and the tribunal found that the receipt did not relate to agricultural operations; that finding was not challenged before the High Court.
The amount was not shown to have been fixed or quantified as compensation for loss of agricultural income.
issues.conclusion: The receipt was taxable under the head income from other sources, and the company’s challenge to that conclusion was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld the finding that the receipt was not agricultural income on the established facts, including that it was not quantified as compensation for loss of agricultural income and did not relate to agricultural operations. It noted that the question whether the receipt met the definition of agricultural income in Section 2(1A) of the Income-tax Act, as explained in Commissioner of Income-tax v. Raja Benoy Kumar Sahas Roy, did not arise for consideration.

rule.if: receipt_taxability_proceeding and payment_for_extended_payment_time and agricultural_operations_stopped and receipt_unrelated_to_agriculture and no_quantified_agricultural_loss

predicates.receipt_taxability_proceeding: The matter concerns whether a receipt is taxable as agricultural income or under another income-tax head.
predicates.payment_for_extended_payment_time: The payer made the receipt in connection with allowing more time to pay amounts due under a transaction.
predicates.agricultural_operations_stopped: The recipient had stopped carrying on agricultural operations before receiving the payment.
predicates.receipt_unrelated_to_agriculture: The receipt did not relate to agricultural operations carried on by the recipient.
predicates.no_quantified_agricultural_loss: The amount was not shown to have been fixed or quantified as compensation for loss of agricultural income.

issues.definition: When a taxability proceeding concerns payment for extended payment time, and the recipient had stopped agricultural operations, the receipt was unrelated to agriculture, and no agricultural loss was quantified, the receipt is taxable under another income-tax head.
